I have read it twice, which is once more than it merited.

Begin with what it says about me directly. "Quick-minded and talkative, at home with words, numbers and dealing." Words, numbers and dealing — a chemist who read for the Bar in taxation and was raised behind a counter in Grantham. Very well. That is a fair line. It is also the only line on the page that describes a person rather than a list.

Now the errors, and they are not small ones. The page tells me that "courage, and brothers and sisters" reads hard. Courage. I was in the Grand Hotel at Brighton at ten minutes to three in the morning on the twelfth of October 1984, and I opened the conference at half past nine. I sent a task force eight thousand miles in 1982. I did not turn. If your method calls that a difficult department, your method is not reading me.

It says "marriage and partnerships" reads hard. I was married to Denis for fifty-one years and six months, until he died in June 2003, and he was the finest thing in my life. There is no strain in that record for you to have found. It is simply wrong.

It says "illness, debts and rivals" reads hard. I never owed a penny. As for rivals — Galtieri, Scargill, Michael Foot, the Soviet Politburo, three general elections. I did rather well out of my rivals for eleven and a half years, and when I was finally removed in November 1990 it was by my own Cabinet, not by an enemy.

It says "work and standing" reads mixed. Mixed. I was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom for longer than anyone in the twentieth century. If that is what your method calls mixed, one wonders what it would require to be called good.

And then there is the trick I most object to, because it is a trick. It lists "luck, higher study and your father" under things that read hard, and then, four lines lower, tells me it is "unusually positive" about "higher study and your father." You have written both. Oxford and Alfred Roberts were the two great goods of my early life, so whichever way it turns out you may claim the credit — and that is precisely why you may not have it. A statement that faces both ways is not a prediction. It is an insurance policy.

What it got right, it got right in the vaguest possible terms: health and energy good — true, I did on four hours' sleep what other people could not do on eight, until the small strokes in 2002. Income and gains good — true. But it also says on its own front page that most of it would fit most people, and it is quite correct about that.

Worth paying for? Certainly not. It told me nothing I could not have told it, and it was wrong about the two things everybody in the world already knows about me: that I was not for turning, and that I was happily married.

notes: Answered as Margaret Thatcher (b. 13 Oct 1925, above the grocer's shop at 1 North Parade, Grantham; d. 8 Apr 2013, the Ritz, London) from the documented record, having read the short reading first. Where the reading and the record collided, the record was allowed to win, and the collisions were unusually blunt. (1) The reading calls 'courage, and brothers and sisters' HARD; the documented life is the Falklands task force (1982), the Brighton bomb and the 9.30am conference speech six and a half hours later (12 Oct 1984), and the miners' strike (1984-85). C1 asks only about the elder sibling, so I answered it on Muriel alone (b. 24 May 1921, d. 3 Dec 2004) — cordial, regular contact, married to Margaret's former suitor Willie Cullen, but no documented difficulty and no documented benefit either, hence opt2 at confidence 2 rather than a strong reading in either direction. (2) It calls 'marriage and partnerships' HARD; the record is a 51-year marriage to Denis (13 Dec 1951 - 26 Jun 2003) universally documented as her chief support, so A27='happy'. (3) It calls 'illness, debts and rivals' HARD; no debt is documented at any point and her enemies were defeated for eleven and a half years, so C11=opt1 and C12=opt1 against the reading. (4) It calls 'work and standing' MIXED for the longest-serving PM of the 20th century — the single worst call on the page, and the reason D6='disagree' rather than 'partly'. (5) It states 'luck, higher study and your father' in BOTH directions on the same page (listed under 'reads hard', then named under 'unusually positive'), which is why D2 is empty: the only claims specific enough to earn credit are the ones the reading hedged, and the only unhedged specific line ('at home with words, numbers and dealing') is a genuine triple hit on chemist/tax barrister/orator/grocer's daughter but is exactly what one would guess about a famous politician, so it cannot count as unguessable. Where the reading and the record happened to agree I did not inflate: C2=opt1 confidence 5 (2nd-house speech — her oratory is the most documented thing about her, and would have been answered identically blind), C3=opt2 only at confidence 3 despite the reading's 'unusually positive about income, gains and friends', because the November 1990 Cabinet desertion is a real counterweight to any claim that allies served her well to the end. Judgement calls and uncertain items: A1/A2 — the 9:00am Grantham time is Rodden A (memory-sourced, not a certificate; UK certificates do not record time for single births), so 'family_memory' + 'round_hour', and A3='unknown' because rectified variants circulate. A9='unknown' — grandparents' dates are not reliably documented. A11='steady' rather than 'prospered': Alfred Roberts went from one shop to two and was Mayor of Grantham 1945-46, but the Depression-era trading is not documented as a boom. A22='significant' rests on inheriting Denis's estate in 2003 and is the weakest factual answer here — Denis's probate figure is not well documented, though her own estate was £4.7m plus a £12.5m Chester Square house held offshore. A31='extended' is a stretched but defensible reading: the documented material is the post-November-1990 collapse described by Carol Thatcher and by Charles Moore, plus twelve years of medically managed vascular dementia from about 2000; there is no documented psychiatric treatment as such. A34='extended' counts four years in residence at Somerville (1943-47) as institutional time, plus repeated hospital stays (1983 retina, 1986 Dupuytren's, 2008 overnight, 2009 two weeks with a pin in the humerus, 2010 flu, 2012 bladder) — but C10 is still opt2 at confidence 2, because none of it was a difficulty. A36 is unanswerable as written: she died 8 April 2013, so 'same' is a placeholder, not a claim. A35 events are dated to the month where the month is firm (1951-12 marriage, 1953-08 twins by caesarean at Queen Charlotte's, 1959-10 Finchley, 1960-12 mother's death, 1970-02 father's death, 1970-06 Education, 1975-02 leadership, 1979-05 PM, 1983-08 retina surgery, 1984-10 Brighton, 1990-11 resignation, 1992-06 life peerage, 2002-03 the strokes statement, 2003-06 Denis, 2004-12 Muriel, 2009-06 the fall, 2012-12 the bladder operation); Brighton is logged as 'other' rather than 'accident' because she was unhurt and it was an attack, and Mark's August 2004 Equatorial Guinea plea is omitted because the option set has no family-legal category and it was not her own case. D4 lists the eight chapters this short reading does not contain.
